summary: A life is told from where its person stood among the children: with an older brother or sister already there, as the first of several, or as the only one.
realLife: Families vary in how many children they have. In the United States the share of mothers who finish with exactly one child doubled over a generation, so more people start their story as the only child, while most start it with an older brother or sister already in the house or as the oldest of several.
sources: Pew Research Center, Family Size Among Mothers: https://www.pewresearch.org/social-trends/2015/05/07/family-size-among-mothers/
American Psychological Association, Only children are often misunderstood: https://www.apa.org/monitor/2024/09/only-children
inGame: the birth chapter's older-sibling, first-born and only-child facts, read from the sibling records by the journal chapter opener (src/director/journal-chapter-open.ts).

turns.what: The older brother or sister dies young, and the person is raised as the oldest.
turns.pulledBy: the older sibling's death record before the person is grown
turns.writesBack: a later chapter that says the person was the oldest left at home, and the Journal reads the family differently

turns.what: A brother or sister is born years after the person, so the only child becomes the oldest of two.
turns.pulledBy: a sibling's birth record in the same household
turns.writesBack: the birth chapter changes from only child to first-born when the later chapters are told looking back
